entities.name: Najib ad-Din Samarqandi
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Najib ad-Din Abu Hamid Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Umar Samarqandi, a preeminent 13th-century Persian physician, epitomized the pinnacle of clinical and pharmacological scholarship during the twilight of the Islamic Golden Age. Hailing from Samarqand in Transoxiana, a vibrant intellectual hub, Samarqandi distinguished himself through a prolific output of medical treatises that systematically codified the accumulated knowledge of previous centuries, integrating Greek, Persian, and Indian medical traditions with astute clinical observation. His work, particularly *Kitab al-Asbab wal-Alamat* (The Book of Causes and Symptoms), became an indispensable reference for practitioners and students, solidifying his reputation as a master diagnostician and therapeutic innovator.

Samarqandi's magnum opus, *Kitab al-Asbab wal-Alamat*, systematically explored diseases from head to toe, detailing their causes (asbab), symptoms (alamat), and rational treatments. This encyclopedic work comprised 25 chapters, each dedicated to specific ailments, offering a meticulously organized framework for clinical diagnosis and management. Beyond this, his *Kitab al-Aghdhiya wal-Ashriba* (Book of Foods and Drinks) delved into dietetics and nutrition, reflecting a holistic understanding of health maintenance and disease prevention, while other works focused on pharmacology and materia medica, often drawing on empirical observations and practical experience.
